name: 08-reduced-model
title: Model Reduction — event-driven vs event-free (speed vs fidelity)

parent_studies.rationale: Performance localized the cost to the per-beat event; this study removes it.
Tests how much hemodynamic fidelity is lost when the pulsatile event layer is dropped.

question:
The per-beat event (E_beat) fires ~205k times over 48 h and is ~99% of the full
model's runtime. Can we replace the events with a continuous mean-hemodynamics model
that still reproduces the sepsis trajectory — and how much faster, and at what cost
to fidelity?
objective:
Build an event-free reduced model (continuous ODEs: pathogen -> inflammation ->
vasodilation + tissue damage -> mean MAP), fit it to the exact severe arm, and
compare it to the full pulsatile model on speed (both engines) and fidelity.
claim:
Removing the per-beat event and the pulsatile layer makes the 48 h sepsis run
~10^7-10^8x faster and closes the COPASI-vs-Tellurium gap. The event-free model
(sources/eventfree_sepsis.ant) runs a 48 h severe course in ~0.2 ms under roadrunner
and ~0.06 ms under COPASI, versus ~2.81 h (roadrunner) and ~3.7 h (COPASI) for the
full model — and with the events gone COPASI is as fast as roadrunner, because the
~3x engine gap was entirely per-event interpreter overhead. Fitted to the exact
severe arm, the reduced model tracks blood pathogen to ~10%, tissue integrity to
~4%, and the mean-MAP decline to ~4% RMSE. It trades fidelity for that speed: it
under-reaches the shock depth (MAP ~80 vs 69.5 mmHg; SVR ~0.78 vs 0.665) and, being
monotonic, misses the full model's baroreflex SVR compensation-then-decompensation,
and it has no pulsatility (no SBP/DBP pulse pressure).

expected_behavior.name: event-free-is-vastly-faster-both-engines
expected_behavior.statement: The event-free model runs a 48 h course orders of magnitude faster than the full pulsatile model under both roadrunner and COPASI, and COPASI is no longer slower than roadrunner.

expected_behavior.name: reduced-model-tracks-the-sepsis-trajectory
expected_behavior.statement: Fitted to the exact severe arm, the event-free model reproduces blood pathogen, tissue integrity, and the mean-MAP decline to within ~10%, with the hemodynamic depth and SVR dynamics as the stated fidelity cost.

findings.summary: Event-free: ~0.2 ms (roadrunner) / ~0.06 ms (COPASI) for 48 h vs ~2.81 h / ~3.7 h full — ~10^7-10^8x, and COPASI = roadrunner (see chart 02).
findings.detail:
The full pulsatile model's ~205k beat events are ~99% of its runtime (study 04:
disabling the event dropped a 60 s COPASI run from 3.8 s to 0.04 s). The event-free
reduced model has no events and is non-stiff, so a 48 h course runs in ~0.2 ms
(roadrunner) and ~0.06 ms (COPASI), against ~2.81 h (roadrunner) and ~3.7 h (COPASI)
for the full model — a ~6x10^7 / ~2x10^8 speedup (out/comparison.json). Crucially,
with the events gone COPASI is as fast as roadrunner (slightly faster here): the
~3x Tellurium-vs-COPASI gap was entirely the per-event interpreter overhead, so it
disappears when there are no events.

findings.summary: The reduced model tracks pathogen (~10%), tissue integrity (~4%), and the MAP decline (~4% RMSE), but under-reaches shock and misses the SVR compensation (chart 01).
findings.detail:
Fitted to the exact severe arm (data/real_trajectories.json), the event-free model
(chart 01, out/comparison.json) tracks blood pathogen to ~10% RMSE, tissue integrity
to ~4%, and the mean-MAP decline to ~4%. The fidelity cost is specific and visible:
the full model's SVR is non-monotonic — it rises to ~1.12 (baroreflex vasoconstriction,
compensation) before crashing to 0.665 (decompensation) — whereas the reduced model's
SVR falls monotonically, so it ends at ~0.78 vs 0.665 and MAP at ~80 vs 69.5 mmHg. It
captures the direction and most of the shock but not its full depth or the
two-phase hemodynamic response, and it has no pulsatility (no SBP/DBP pulse pressure).
So the reduced model is a screening-grade surrogate for the slow sepsis outcome, not a
replacement for the pulsatile physiology.
findings.statement: The event-free model is a speed/fidelity trade, not a free lunch: ~10^7x faster and engine-agnostic, at the cost of hemodynamic depth, the baroreflex SVR dynamics, and pulsatility.
findings.explanation: The removed structure and the lost fidelity are the same thing. The per-beat event is what makes the full model both expensive (205k root-finds + reinits, ~99% of runtime) and detailed (beat-to-beat pulse pressure, and the baroreflex that drives SVR up before it collapses). Dropping it buys ~10^7x speed and removes the per-event interpreter overhead that made COPASI ~3x slower — so the engines converge. It costs the pulsatile layer (no SBP/DBP) and the compensation-then-decompensation SVR trajectory, which a monotonic mean-hemodynamics model cannot represent; hence the reduced model under-reaches the shock depth even after fitting. The honest placement: this is a fast screening surrogate for the slow sepsis outcome (pathogen, tissue integrity, mean-MAP trend), useful where thousands of runs or interactive exploration matter, and the full pulsatile model remains the reference where hemodynamic depth, pulse pressure, or the baroreflex dynamics matter. A closer fit would need a two-phase (compensation) hemodynamic term, a noted follow-up.
